units.en: Sun Quan and his son owed Han little; Liu Bei and his ministers raised themselves from Zhuo.
units.literal: Sun Quan and his son owed no obvious grant of Han favor; Liu Bei and his ministers rose on their own from Zhuo commandery.

units.zh: 得之不謝於家世，失之無損於功名，適當逐鹿之秋，何惜華蟲之服。
units.en: Winning the realm did not depend on pedigree; losing it did not stain their names—it was the season of chasing the deer, and court dress meant little.
units.literal: Gaining the realm owed nothing to family standing; losing it did not harm their fame—this was the season of contending for the deer; why cling to court robes?

units.zh: 惟仆累朝席寵，奕世輸忠，忝佩訓詞，粗存家法。
units.en: I alone have been favored through many reigns and loyal through generations; I am unworthy of your counsel, yet I still keep my house's rule.
units.literal: Only your servant has enjoyed favor through many reigns and given loyalty through generations; I am shamed to wear your instruction yet still keep the family law.

units.zh: 善博奕者惟先守道，治蹊田者不可奪牛。
units.en: A good chess player keeps the rules first; a man who tends his own field must not take another's ox.
units.literal: A good player of chess first keeps the Way; one who tends the border field must not seize another's ox.

units.zh: 誓於此生，靡敢失節，仰憑廟勝，早殄寇讎。
units.en: I swear never to break faith in this life and trust the ancestral shrine's blessing to destroy the enemy soon.
units.literal: I swear in this life never to break faith, relying on the ancestral temple's victory to destroy the foe soon.

units.zh: 如其事與願違，則共臧洪遊於地下，亦無恨矣。
units.en: If heaven wills otherwise, I would rather keep Zang Hong company in the grave and feel no regret.
units.literal: If affairs go against my wish, then to wander underground with Zang Hong would be no regret.

units.zh: 惟公社稷元勳，嵩、衡降祉，鎮九州之上地，負一代之鴻才，合於此時，自求多福。
units.en: You alone are the state's founding pillar; fortune falls on you from the sacred peaks; you hold the heartland of the realm and bear the talent of the age—seize this moment and secure your own blessing.
units.literal: Only you, sir, are a founding minister of the state; Song and Heng send down blessing; you hold the upper lands of the Nine Provinces and bear the great talent of an age—fit this moment and seek your own blessing.

units.zh: 所承良訊，非仆深心，天下其謂我何，有國非吾節也。
units.en: Your generous proposal is not my true mind; what would the world say of me? To take a kingdom is not my way.
units.literal: The fine message you offer is not my inmost heart; what would the world say of me? To hold a realm is not my principle.

units.zh: 淒淒孤懇，此不盡陳。
units.en: My lonely plea is full of grief; I cannot say all of it.
units.literal: My solitary plea is sorrowful; this cannot fully be told.

units.zh: 五月，梁祖遣其將康懷英率兵十萬圍潞州，懷英驅率士眾，築壘環城，城中音信斷絕。
units.en: In the fifth month the Liang Founder sent Kang Huaiying with a hundred thousand men to besiege Lu; Huaiying drove his troops to ring the city with camps and cut off all news from within.
units.literal: Fifth month, the Liang Founder sent his general Kang Huaiying with a hundred thousand troops to besiege Lu Prefecture; Huaiying drove the soldiers, built stockades ringing the city, and word within the walls was cut off.

units.zh: 武皇遣周德威將兵赴援，德威軍於餘吾，率先鋒挑戰，日有俘獲，懷英不敢即戰。
units.en: Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei to relieve the city; Dewei camped at Yuyu, led the van in daily skirmishes, and took prisoners every day; Huaiying would not fight a pitched battle.
units.literal: Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei with troops to relieve the city; Dewei camped at Yuyu, led the vanguard to challenge daily, and took captives each day; Huaiying dared not give battle at once.

units.zh: 梁祖以懷英無功，乃以李思安代之。
units.en: Because Huaiying had achieved nothing, the Liang Founder replaced him with Li Si'an.
units.literal: The Liang Founder, because Huaiying had no success, replaced him with Li Si'an.

units.zh: 思安引軍將營於潞城，周德威以五千騎搏之，梁軍大敗，斬首千餘級。
units.en: Si'an moved to camp at Lucheng; Zhou Dewei struck with five thousand horse, routed the Liang army, and took more than a thousand heads.
units.literal: Si'an led troops to camp at Lucheng; Zhou Dewei with five thousand cavalry engaged them; the Liang army was greatly defeated and more than a thousand heads were taken.

units.zh: 思安退保堅壁，別築外壘，謂之「夾塞」，以抗我之援軍。
units.en: Si'an fell back behind stout walls and built outer camps called the "Twin Forts" to block our relief.
units.literal: Si'an withdrew to hold a strong wall and separately built outer stockades called the "twin forts" to block our relief army.

units.zh: 梁祖調發山東之民以供饋運，德威日以輕騎掩之，運路艱阻，眾心益恐。
units.en: The Liang Founder drafted the people of Shandong for convoys; Dewei sent light horse against them daily; the routes grew perilous and morale sank.
units.literal: The Liang Founder mobilized the people of Shandong for supply transport; Dewei daily sent light cavalry to harry them; the supply routes grew hard and hearts grew more fearful.

units.zh: 李思安乃自東南山口築夾道，連接夾寨，以通饋運，自是梁軍堅保夾塞。
units.en: Li Si'an then built a walled road from the southeast pass to link the twin forts and keep supplies moving; after that the Liang army held the forts in strength.
units.literal: Li Si'an then built a walled road from the southeastern mountain pass linking the twin forts to open supply transport; from then on the Liang army held the twin forts firmly.

units.zh: 冬十月，武皇有疾，是時晉陽城無故自壞，占者惡之。
units.en: In the tenth month of winter Wuhuang fell ill; the walls of Jinyang collapsed for no reason, and diviners called it a bad sign.
units.literal: Tenth month of winter, Wuhuang fell ill; at that time the walls of Jinyang collapsed without cause, and diviners took it as ill omen.

units.zh: 天祐五年正月戊子朔，武皇疾革。
units.en: On the new moon of the first month of Tianyou 5 Wuhuang grew deathly ill.
units.literal: On the wuzi new moon of the first month of Tianyou 5, Wuhuang's illness turned critical.

units.zh: 辛卯，崩於晉陽，年五十三。
units.en: On xinmao he died at Jinyang, aged fifty-three.
units.literal: On xinmao he died at Jinyang, aged fifty-three.

units.zh: 遣令薄葬，發喪後二十七日除服。
units.en: He ordered a plain burial and that mourning dress end twenty-seven days after the funeral.
units.literal: His testament ordered a plain burial and mourning dress laid aside twenty-seven days after the funeral.

units.zh: 莊宗即位，追諡武皇帝，廟號太祖，陵在雁門。
units.en: Zhuangzong posthumously named him Martial Emperor, gave him the temple name Taizu, and buried him at Yanmen.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he posthumously titled him Martial Emperor, temple name Taizu, tomb at Yanmen.

units.zh: 《五代史補》：太祖武皇，本朱耶赤心之後，沙陁部人也。
units.en: The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says Wuhuang Taizu was descended from Zhuoye Chixin and was of the Shatuo tribe.
units.literal: The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says: Taizu Wuhuang was originally of the Zhuoye Chixin line, a man of the Shatuo tribe.

units.zh: 其先生於雕窠中，酋長以其異生，諸族傳養之，遂以「諸爺」為氏，言非一父所養也。
units.en: An ancestor was born in an eagle's nest; the chieftain, seeing the omen, had the clans rear him by turns, and they took "Zhu Ye" as the clan name—"not one father's child."
units.literal: His ancestor was born in an eagle's nest; the chieftain, because the birth was strange, had the clans raise him in turn, and they took "Zhu Ye" as the clan name, meaning not raised by one father.

units.zh: 其後言訛，以「諸」為「朱」，以 「爺」為「耶」。
units.en: Later the name was corrupted: "Zhu-ye" became the Zhu and Ye of his surname.
units.literal: Later the name was corrupted: "Zhu-ye" became the Zhu and Ye of his surname.

units.zh: 至太祖生，眇一目，長而驍勇，善騎射，所向無敵，時謂之「獨眼龍」，大為部落所疾。
units.en: Taizu was born with one blind eye; grown he was fierce, a master of horse and bow, unbeaten in battle, and men called him the "One-Eyed Dragon"—much hated in the tribe.
units.literal: When Taizu was born he had one blind eye; grown he was fierce and brave, skilled in horse and bow, unmatched wherever he went; men called him the "One-Eyed Dragon," and the tribes greatly resented him.

units.zh: 太祖恐禍及，遂舉族歸唐，授雲州刺史，賜姓李，名克用。
units.en: Fearing harm, he led his clan to Tang, was made prefect of Yun, given the surname Li, and named Keyong.
units.literal: Taizu feared disaster would reach him, led his whole clan to submit to Tang, was made prefect of Yunzhou, granted the surname Li, and named Keyong.

units.zh: 黃巢犯長安，自北引兵赴難，功成，遂拜太原節度使，封晉王。
units.en: When Huang Chao took Chang'an he marched from the north to save the throne; for his service he became military commissioner of Taiyuan and Prince of Jin.
units.literal: When Huang Chao struck Chang'an he led troops south from the north to the rescue; when the work succeeded he was made military commissioner of Taiyuan and enfeoffed Prince of Jin.

units.zh: 武皇之有河東也，威聲大振。
units.en: Once Wuhuang held Hedong his fame as a warrior soared.
units.literal: When Wuhuang held Hedong his martial renown greatly rose.

units.zh: 淮南楊行密常恨識其狀貌，因使畫工詐為商賈，往河東寫之。
units.en: Yang Xingmi of Huainan, who had never seen his face, sent a painter disguised as a merchant to Hedong to capture his likeness.
units.literal: Huainan's Yang Xingmi often regretted not knowing his appearance, and therefore sent a painter disguised as a merchant to Hedong to paint him.

units.zh: 畫工到，未幾，人有知其謀者，擒之。
units.en: The painter had barely arrived when someone uncovered the plot and seized him.
units.literal: When the painter arrived, before long someone knew the plot and seized him.

units.zh: 武皇初甚怒，既而謂所親曰：「且吾素眇一目，試召之使寫，觀其所為如何。」
units.en: Wuhuang was furious at first, then told his intimates, "I have been blind in one eye for years—bring him in and see what he paints."
units.literal: Wuhuang at first was very angry, then said to those close to him: "I have long had one blind eye—summon him to paint and see what he does."

units.zh: 及至，武皇按膝厲聲曰：「淮南使汝來寫吾真，必畫工之尤也，寫吾不及十分，即價下便是死汝之所矣。」
units.en: When the man came, Wuhuang struck his knee and thundered, "Huainan sent you to paint me—you must be their best. Fall short by a tenth and that lowered price is your death."
units.literal: When he came, Wuhuang pressed his knee and said in a harsh voice: "Huainan sent you to paint my likeness—you must be a master painter. Paint me less than perfect and the lowered price is where you die."

units.zh: 畫工再拜下筆。
units.en: The painter bowed again and began to paint.
units.literal: The painter bowed again and set brush to silk.

units.zh: 時方盛暑，武皇執八角扇，因寫扇角半遮其面。
units.en: It was midsummer; Wuhuang held an eight-sided fan, and the painter hid half his face behind the fan in the picture.
units.literal: It was the height of summer; Wuhuang held an eight-cornered fan, and the painter therefore painted the fan corner half hiding his face.

units.zh: 武皇曰：「汝諂吾也。」
units.en: Wuhuang said, "You flatter me."
units.literal: Wuhuang said: "You flatter me."

units.zh: 遽使別寫之，又應聲下筆，畫其臂弓撚箭之狀，仍微合一目以觀箭之曲直，武皇大喜，因厚賂金帛遣之。
units.en: He ordered another portrait; the painter worked at once, showing him with bow on arm and arrow drawn, one eye narrowed to sight the shaft; Wuhuang was delighted, gave him gold and silk, and sent him away.
units.literal: He at once had another painting made; again the brush answered at once, painting him with bow on arm twisting an arrow, still slightly closing one eye to judge the arrow's curve; Wuhuang was greatly pleased and gave gold and silk in rich reward before sending him away.

units.zh: 《五代史闕文》：世傳武皇臨薨，以三矢付莊宗曰：「一矢討劉仁恭，汝不先下幽州，河南未可圖也。
units.en: The 《Lost Chapters of the History of the Five Dynasties》 says: Tradition holds that on his deathbed Wuhuang gave Zhuangzong three arrows, saying, "One to punish Liu Rengong—you must take Youzhou before you can dream of Henan.
units.literal: The 《Lost Chapters of the History of the Five Dynasties》 says: Tradition holds that as Wuhuang lay dying he gave Zhuangzong three arrows, saying: "One arrow to punish Liu Rengong—you cannot take Henan until you first take Youzhou.

units.zh: 一矢擊契丹，且曰阿保機與吾把臂而盟，結為兄弟，誓復唐家社稷，今背約附賊，汝必伐之。
units.en: One to strike the Khitan—Abaoji swore brotherhood with me and vowed to restore Tang; now he breaks faith and joins the traitor—you must attack him.
units.literal: One arrow to strike the Khitan—and he said Abaoji clasped arms with me and swore brotherhood, vowing to restore the Tang realm; now he breaks the pact and joins the bandit—you must attack him.

units.zh: 一矢滅朱溫，汝能成吾誌，死無憾矣！」
units.en: One to destroy Zhu Wen—if you fulfill my will I die content!"
units.literal: One arrow to destroy Zhu Wen—if you can fulfill my will I die without regret!"

units.zh: 莊宗藏三矢於武皇廟庭。
units.en: Zhuangzong kept the three arrows in Wuhuang's temple court.
units.literal: Zhuangzong stored the three arrows in the court of Wuhuang's temple.

units.zh: 及討劉仁恭，命幕吏以少牢告廟，請一矢，盛以錦囊，使親將負之以為前驅。
units.en: When he marched on Liu Rengong he had a clerk offer sacrifice at the temple, took one arrow in a brocade bag, and had a trusted general carry it before the van.
units.literal: When he campaigned against Liu Rengong he ordered a staff officer to report to the temple with a young victim, took one arrow, placed it in a brocade bag, and had a trusted general carry it before the van.

units.zh: 凱旋之日，隨俘馘納矢於太廟。
units.en: On the day of victory he brought the arrow back with prisoners and spoils to the Grand Temple.
units.literal: On the day of triumph he presented the arrow with the captives and spoils at the Grand Temple.

units.zh: 伐契丹，滅朱氏亦如之。
units.en: He did the same against the Khitan and in destroying the Zhu house.
units.literal: Against the Khitan and in destroying the Zhu clan he did the same.

units.zh: 又，武皇眇一目，謂之「獨眼龍。」
units.en: It adds that Wuhuang had one blind eye and was called the "One-Eyed Dragon."
units.literal: Further, Wuhuang had one blind eye and was called the "One-Eyed Dragon."

units.zh: 性喜殺，左右有小過失，必置於死。
units.en: He loved killing; a small slip by an attendant meant death.
units.literal: He delighted in killing; attendants who made small faults were always put to death.

units.zh: 初諱眇，人無敢犯者，嘗令寫真，畫工即為撚箭之狀，微瞑一目，圖成而進，武皇大悅，賜予甚厚。）
units.en: His blind eye was once taboo; when he ordered a portrait the painter showed him drawing a bow with one eye narrowed; Wuhuang was delighted and rewarded him richly.)
units.literal: At first his blind eye was taboo and none dared mention it; once he ordered his portrait painted, and the painter at once showed him twisting an arrow, one eye slightly closed; when the picture was done and presented Wuhuang was greatly pleased and gave a rich reward.)

units.zh: 史臣曰：武皇肇跡陰山，赴難唐室，逐豺狼於魏闕，殄氛祲於秦川，賜姓受封，奄有汾、晉，可謂有功矣。
units.en: The historian writes: Wuhuang rose from Yinshan, saved the Tang court, drove wolves from the capital, and cleared rebellion from Qinchuan; he took a surname, a fief, and held Fen and Jin—this was merit.
units.literal: The historian says: Wuhuang began his track at Yinshan, rushed to aid the Tang house, drove wolves from the Wei gate, and extinguished evil vapors in Qinchuan; he received surname and fief and held Fen and Jin—this may be called merit.

units.zh: 然雖茂勤王之績，而非無震主之威。
units.en: Yet for all his zeal in the king's service, he also inspired fear in his lord.
units.literal: Yet though his service to the throne was abundant, he was not without awe that shook the ruler.

units.zh: 及朱旗屯渭曲之師，俾翠輦有石門之幸，比夫桓、文之輔周室，無乃有所愧乎！
units.en: When Zhu armies camped on the Wei bend and the imperial carriage met Shimen's fate, beside Huan and Wen who upheld Zhou, he had reason to blush.
units.literal: When Zhu banners camped at Weiqu and the green carriage knew the fortune of Shimen, compared with Huan and Wen aiding the Zhou house, was he not somewhat shamed!

units.zh: 洎失援於蒲、絳，久垂翅於並、汾，若非嗣子之英才，豈有興王之茂業。
units.en: When he lost Pu and Jiang and languished at Bing and Fen, without an able son there would have been no founding reign.
units.literal: By the time he lost aid at Pu and Jiang and long hung his wings at Bing and Fen, had his heir not been a man of talent, how could there have been a founding king's great work.

units.zh: 矧累功積德，未比於周文，創業開基，尚虧於魏祖。
units.en: His piled merit never matched King Wen, and his founding fell short of Cao Cao.
units.literal: Moreover his piled merit and stored virtue did not equal King Wen of Zhou, and in founding a realm and opening a line he still fell short of Wei's founder.

units.zh: 追諡為「武」，斯亦幸焉！
units.en: That he was posthumously styled "Martial" was itself a mercy.
units.literal: To be posthumously styled "Martial" was also a piece of fortune.
